# Goban Studio v5.0.0

v5 is about depth: the rules you play by, opponents that play like people,
reviews that see the whole game, a course that goes past the basics, and
your data and updates in your own hands.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation (KataGo publishes no ARM64 Windows build).

## Rules

- **Japanese, Chinese or Korean rules**, per game (New game → More options)
  or as your default (Settings). **Japanese stays the default for everyone.**
- Chinese rules count area (stones plus territory, komi 7.5; White receives
  one point per handicap stone). Korean rules count like Japanese.
- Seki is scored correctly under each ruleset. KataGo analyses, plays and
  marks dead stones under the game's own rules.
- SGF records declaring Japanese, Chinese or Korean rules open and keep their
  ruleset; other rulesets are still explained and refused rather than
  re-scored.

## Opponents (optional downloads)

- **Human-style opponent**: with KataGo's human model (99 MB, downloaded
  only when you choose it in Settings), each level plays like a person of
  that strength — human shape, human mistakes — instead of a strong engine
  with random slips.
- **Stronger network** (48 MB, optional): used for analysis, review, hints,
  counting and the top level.
- Both come from KataGo's official GitHub releases at pinned addresses, are
  verified with a pinned SHA-256 before use, resume after an interruption,
  live in the app's data folder and can be removed again. Without them the
  app is unchanged and fully offline.

## Review

- **The game in three phases**: points lost, mistakes and blunders, and
  accuracy in the opening, middle game and endgame, with three takeaways
  that link to the moves.
- **Trends** on Today: your recent rated games, where the points go, and
  whether each phase and each kind of mistake is getting better.
- **A record you can edit**: comments and marks (triangle, square, circle,
  cross, letters) on any move, a variation tree, promote or delete
  variations — saved back to your library and written to SGF. Unknown SGF
  properties are kept on the way through.

## Learning

- **An intermediate course**: 5 new units and 26 lessons — opening
  principles, basic joseki, good and bad shape, endgame (sente and gote,
  counting simple endgame moves), and fighting. Players who already know the
  game start there.
- **509 problems** (up from 262), every one proved by the solver under
  real-board rules. Eye shape, false eyes, ko, seki and big-eye races are no
  longer thin; seki now has easy entry problems; 28 classic shapes.
- Topic pages fold by difficulty; a problem shows its difficulty, theme and
  your record with it; problem windows take the shape of the problem.
- The course is a map: every unit's progress at a glance.

## Your data and updates

- **Backup**: Settings → Export backup… saves settings, progress, level,
  mistake drills and every game in one file; Restore from backup… on
  another computer.
- **In-app updates**: when Check for updates… finds a newer version,
  Download and install fetches this computer's package and the release's
  `SHA256SUMS`, verifies and unpacks it, and Restart to update swaps it in —
  and puts the old version back automatically if the new one does not start.
  Where the app cannot replace itself (a read-only folder), it says why and
  offers the download page.

## Interface

- Today shows this week (games, problems, lessons, level change) and recent
  trends; captured stones drift towards the lid; opening tips for newer
  players on larger boards; thumbnails follow the board you chose.

## Known limits

- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet); the table above says
  what this build is. The update checksum guards against damaged or wrong
  downloads; it is not a signature.
- The human-style levels and the stronger network were measured in only a
  few dozen games (`docs/strength.md`); the labels come from the v4
  calibration of the standard levels.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test, a strong player's review of
  the course and problems, and native-speaker review of the Chinese, Korean
  and Japanese text (`docs/usability.md`, `docs/l10n/`).
- Endgame problems with exact counting, and the leaning attack and sabaki
  lessons, are not included; they need a counting mode in the solver and
  content we could state with confidence.

## Your data

Everything from v4 carries over. Games without a declared ruleset stay
Japanese.
